title: Complexity of Classical Acceleration for $\ell_1$-Regularized PageRank
claim: Across increasing boundary sizes, the graph's block structure stays consistent: dense core, banded boundary, dense exterior, and sparse cross-region links.
layout: 5 panels in one row, shared log-scale colorbar, dashed block dividers
description: A single row of five square heatmaps shows the adjacency matrix of a constructed graph for boundary sizes B=320, 400, 600, 800 and 1000. A shared vertical colorbar on the right (magma, log scale from 1e-4 to 1e0, labeled 'edge density') applies to all panels. Each panel is divided by dashed blue lines into core, boundary and exterior blocks. A large pale-yellow dense block fills the upper right (the exterior). A small dense square sits at the corner (the clique). A bright yellow diagonal band, the circulant boundary, runs through the middle block. Thin orange diagonal stripes mark sparse cross-region links, and red strips run along the edges. As B grows, the exterior block shrinks and the boundary band gets longer. White marks density below 1e-4.
caption: Adjacency density. For each boundary size $|\mathcal{B}|$ we visualize the adjacency matrix via a binned edge-density heatmap (bin size $20$), where each pixel shows the fraction of possible edges between a pair of bins (log-scaled; colormap magma with white below $10^{-4}$). Dashed lines mark the core | boundary | exterior block boundaries. The plots show the clique (upper-left block), the boundary circulant band, the nearly dense exterior block, and the sparse cross-region interfaces.
abstract: We study the degree-weighted work required to compute $\ell_1$-regularized PageRank using the standard accelerated proximal-gradient method (FISTA). For non-accelerated methods (ISTA), the best known worst-case work is $\widetilde{O}((Î±Ï)^{-1})$, where $Î±$ is the teleportation parameter and $Ï$ is the $\ell_1$-regularization parameter. It is not known whether classical acceleration methods can improve $1/Î±$ to $1/\sqrtÎ±$ while preserving the $1/Ï$ locality scaling, or whether they can be asymptotically worse. For FISTA, we show a negative result by constructing a family of instances for which standard FISTA is asymptotically worse than ISTA. On the positive side, we analyze FISTA on a slightly over-regularized objective and show that, under a confinement condition, all spurious activations remain inside a boundary set $\mathcal{B}$. This yields a bound consisting of an accelerated $(Ï\sqrtÎ±)^{-1}\log(Î±/\varepsilon)$ term plus a boundary overhead $\sqrt{vol(\mathcal{B})}/(ÏÎ±^{3/2})$. We also provide graph-structural sufficient conditions that imply such confinement.
